_comment: Weekly subscriber and view snapshot per channel. Trend matters more than level: the numbers here are small enough that any single figure is noise, so the point of this file is the shape over weeks. Monetisation for new creators needs 1,000 subscribers and 20,000,000 Shorts views in 90 days (~220k views/day), which no amount of extra thin uploads reaches — the file exists to show whether quality-led publishing moves it at all. publicVideos falls as the cleanup retires the back catalogue; that is intended and is not a loss of reach. Instagram is not covered: the Composio Instagram connection publishes but the account is not exposed for insights reads here.

snapshots.note: First snapshot — no trend yet. publicVideos recorded pre-cleanup; batch 1 retired 10 immediately after this read. yt-bbmw0 has 0 reels live: every one of its 72 public videos is the old format.

snapshots.source: Composio YOUTUBE_GET_CHANNEL_STATISTICS; reelsLive derived from scripts/data/published.json (themeId=reel entries with a youtubeId)
snapshots.note: Two weeks after the first snapshot (2026-08-18 to 2026-09-01), views on yt-bbmw0 dropped from 664 to 544 and publicVideos from 72 to 62; both are the cleanup doing its job, not a loss of reach: views only accrue on videos while they are public, and unlisting a low-performing back-catalogue video removes its stale view count from this total along with the risk it carried. yt-bbm0902 held roughly flat (161 to 91 views is the same effect on a smaller base, plus one further Class A unlist mid-period). Subscriber count moved from a combined 1 to 2, which at this scale is noise, not signal — nowhere near a trend yet. publicVideos here is pre-batch-3: this week's 10-video Class C unlist (see cleanup-log.json) lands after this read, so the next snapshot should show yt-bbmw0 publicVideos closer to 52. reelsLive is a floor, not a ceiling: it only counts uploads this repo's own published.json has a record of, and predates a full per-video format audit against the live channel.
